record_protocol.question: Does routing already-allocated records through the new prepare/commit transaction account for the confirmed Native record-create regression?
record_protocol.intervention: Diagnostic-only replacement of mmay_managed_publish_object with its exact parent implementation; retain candidate string constructor, prepare/commit API, collector, all runtime dependencies and generated benchmark C. No production edits.
record_protocol.method: Compile both wrapper versions against the same candidate runtime archive and the same generated C object. Compare both relinked diagnostics and the frozen candidate/control with 3 warmups and 11 rotating fresh-process samples, in two independent series. Preserve original arguments/stdout/corpus hashes/64MiB. Counter-only copies establish publication kinds and GC counts. No diagnostic performance result accepts production.
record_protocol.interpretation: A repeatable reduction versus the relinked candidate supports the publication-path hypothesis. Compiler/code-layout effects remain possible; do not overclaim a unique instruction-level cause. An unchanged result requires another diagnosis before selecting a code change.
record_protocol.must_wait_for: measurement.json terminal rejected-full; no overlap with acceptance timing

method_correction.reason: The first diagnostic retains each full host snapshot inside an ever-growing in-memory result and rewrites it after every process. The final result is 35,332,396 bytes; series duration grows from 42.8s to 88.3s and small-process latencies rise. This is a measurement-harness confound, not accepted speed evidence. Preserve the entire first result.
method_correction.change: Write full host snapshots to an append-only JSONL journal and keep only their UTC in the compact result. Keep all binaries, original arguments, counters, 3 warmups and 11 samples, two series and balanced participant order unchanged. Repeat this diagnostic only; do not change or repeat the rejected acceptance series.
method_correction.purpose: Bound parent memory/serialization overhead for a more reliable publication-path diagnosis.

off_protocol.question: Why does rejected OFF Dijkstra have a repeatable 2.2s/2.7s distribution while its exact control stays near 2.2s?
off_protocol.method: Twelve alternating pairs on the original workload/arguments. Six pairs collect a one-second 1ms macOS sample of each exact owned VM process; six have no sampling. Record wait4 user/system CPU, faults and context switches for the VM child alone, plus sampled stacks and image addresses. No source, binary, input, limit or execution fuel change. No performance acceptance or favorable rerun is derived from these diagnostic observations.
off_protocol.interpretation: CPU time versus elapsed distinguishes extra CPU work from descheduling; sampled paths may localize it. Profiles are diagnostic and can perturb execution. ASLR/layout correlation is a hypothesis only.
